chunks: Therefore, it is upon you to strive, make effort, equip yourself, get ready and provide yourself from the place of provision.

And let not the life of this world deceive you as it deceived those before you among the past people and by-gone periods -- those who extracted its milk, benefited from its neglectfulness, passed a long time and turned its new things into old (by living long).

key_terms.التَّزَوُّد: Providing oneself with provisions (spiritual or material) for the journey
key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: The worldly life, often contrasted with the hereafter
key_terms.الْجِدّ: Diligence, earnestness, or striving in religious and worldly affairs
key_terms.الْقُرُون: Centuries, eras, or periods of time

ai.seo_question: What does Nahj al-Balagha say about the virtue of diligence and the deception of the world?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) frames diligence (jid) not merely as productivity but as a spiritual imperative for accumulating provisions (tazawwud) before the inevitable arrival of death. This warning against the deceptive allure of dunya echoes the Shia tradition of balancing worldly engagement with eschatological awareness, urging believers to learn from the fate of past nations who were consumed by their own temporal gains.
